evals.prompt: Define SLOs for our educational platform. Key user journeys: student login (must complete in <2s), quiz submission (must succeed 99.9% of time), and content loading (LCP <2.5s). Current error budget is unknown.
evals.expected_output: Defines SLIs and SLOs for each journey, calculates error budgets, proposes burn-rate alerts, and defines escalation policies.
assertions: Defines specific SLIs (Service Level Indicators) for each of the 3 user journeys
Sets measurable SLO targets with corresponding error budgets
Proposes burn-rate alerting to detect when error budget consumption is too fast

evals.prompt: Our alerting system fires 200+ alerts per day but only 5% are actionable. The on-call team is suffering from alert fatigue. Diagnose and fix the alert noise problem.
evals.expected_output: Analyzes alert rules for overly sensitive thresholds, proposes alert consolidation, severity-based routing, and signal-to-noise optimization.
assertions: Identifies overly sensitive thresholds or redundant rules as the noise source
Proposes alert consolidation and deduplication strategies
Recommends severity-based routing so only critical alerts page on-call

evals.prompt: Design a distributed tracing strategy for our microservices (8 services, 3 databases, 2 external APIs). We have no tracing today and debugging production issues takes hours.
evals.expected_output: Proposes OpenTelemetry instrumentation, trace propagation strategy, sampling policy, and integration with visualization tools like Jaeger or Tempo.
assertions: Recommends OpenTelemetry for instrumentation with specific SDK guidance
Designs trace context propagation across all 8 services, databases, and external APIs
Proposes a sampling strategy that balances cost with debugging visibility

evals.prompt: Design a chaos engineering experiment to validate our platform's resilience. We want to test: database failover, API latency injection, and pod failure recovery. This is our first chaos experiment.
evals.expected_output: Proposes a graduated chaos engineering plan starting with safe experiments, defines steady state hypotheses, blast radius controls, and abort conditions.
assertions: Proposes a graduated approach starting with the least risky experiment
Defines steady-state hypotheses and expected behavior for each experiment
Includes blast radius controls and automatic abort conditions for safety

evals.prompt: Our observability stack has blind spots: we monitor API response times and error rates but have no visibility into database query performance, background job health, or third-party API reliability. Identify and fill the gaps.
evals.expected_output: Maps current observability coverage, identifies the 3 blind spots, proposes specific instrumentation for each, and designs unified dashboards.
assertions: Identifies the 3 specific blind spots: database queries, background jobs, and third-party APIs
Proposes specific instrumentation for each blind spot (query timing, job metrics, API health checks)
Designs a unified dashboard or correlation strategy to link all observability signals

should_trigger: Define SLOs and error budgets for our platform's key user journeys
We have too many alerts and alert fatigue, help reduce the noise
Design a distributed tracing strategy for our microservices
Plan our first chaos engineering experiment to test resilience
We have observability blind spots in database and background jobs
should_not_trigger: Design a Terraform module for our AWS infrastructure
Review this FastAPI endpoint for performance issues
Fine-tune an LLM for our educational assistant
Build a data pipeline with dbt for student analytics
